observation.visible_scene: Two clear drinking glasses sit side by side on a white surface in front of a sheet of printed text. The left glass holds yellow liquid with a thin orange layer settled at the bottom; the right glass holds a smaller amount of green liquid. A single black ribbed 'bendy' straw arches over the rims, its left end submerged in the yellow liquid and its right end submerged in the green liquid, forming a siphon-shaped loop. A translucent white concentric-circle ripple graphic is overlaid near the apex of the straw arch.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the yellow surface in the left glass gradually falls (the liquid level lowers), while the green surface in the right glass gradually rises, i.e. the left column shortens and the right column lengthens relative to their first and last frames.
The orange sediment layer at the bottom of the left glass and the small green droplet on the upper-left rim remain in place throughout.
The straw arch keeps the same shape and position; only the liquid levels inside the glasses change.
The white concentric-circle overlay near the top of the straw pulses, expanding and contracting and shifting slightly frame to frame; this is a graphic effect, not physical motion of the apparatus.
The printed-paper background and the glasses' positions stay essentially fixed, indicating the camera is largely static.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the siphon was already primed before this segment and whether the level change continues after the last frame are not shown.
The cause of the level change (siphoning, evaporation, or added/removed liquid) is not directly visible.
What lies below the visible rims of the glasses and behind the paper is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact rate and mechanism of the liquid transfer cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
A faint thin vertical line in the right glass may be a reflection or a separate object; it is not clearly resolved.
Minor apparent shifts of the background text could be camera jitter or paper movement; this is not certain.
